html:
Uruguay is a small country on the east bank of the Río de la Plata in South America, independent since 1828.

The land, then called the Banda Oriental, was fought over by Spain and Portugal. Spain founded Montevideo in 1726 as part of what became the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata. In the wars of independence José Gervasio Artigas led the fight for local self-rule, but Portuguese and then Brazilian forces took the land. The Cisplatine War between Brazil and Argentina ended in 1828 with Uruguay as a buffer state between them.

For decades two parties, the Blancos and the Colorados, fought civil wars. Uruguay sided with Brazil and Argentina in the Paraguayan War. Then came a long run of peace and prosperity:

  • Immigrants from Spain and Italy filled Montevideo, and beef and wool exports made the country rich.
  • President José Batlle y Ordóñez, early in the 1900s, built one of the first welfare states in the Americas.
  • Uruguay hosted and won the first football World Cup in 1930, and won again in Brazil in 1950.

Economic decline and the Tupamaros guerrillas were followed by a military dictatorship from 1973 to 1985. Since then Uruguay has been one of the most stable democracies in Latin America. Under José Mujica, a former guerrilla, it became the first country to fully legalise cannabis in 2013.
sum: Uruguay is a small country on the east bank of the Río de la Plata in South America, independent since 1828.
